model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on common equity, hybrid coupons charged in the flow

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (core net revenue FY2022-FY2025, from the 20-F income statements)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.3% vs EPS 5yr 18.4% (>30% apart): the EPS base year FY2020 was the COVID-provision trough (KRW 1,742/share) and FY2022-25 EPS is flat (-1.6% 3yr), while owners' equity growth is inflated by AT1 hybrid issuance (KRW 2.6tn -> 3.8tn) and OCI. Neither is a forward growth measure; the projection is driven from core net revenue, whose 3yr CAGR (3.7%) brackets the FY2027 base growth of 5% (NIM uplift + insurance) fading to 2.5%.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs to FY2025 from WF_Metrics.csv (equity attributable to owners incl. hybrids, EPS per common share) and the 20-F income statements (core net revenue: FY2021 8,765.7; FY2022 10,566.8; FY2025 11,779.6). Revenue 5yr not computed (FY2020 fee/dividend lines not in the extracted comparatives); 4yr from FY2021 shown instead and is flattered by the 2022 rate-driven NII jump. FCF CAGRs not meaningful for a bank (OCF swings by tens of trillions with deposit and trading flows).

scenario_narratives.base: Value-up delivered at a discount to target: ROE on common equity ~9-9.5% (vs the 10% ambition), NIM uplift from the 2026 BOK hikes, fee income compounding, insurers merged H2 2027, credit costs low-40bps, CET1 held ~13.7% with capital above target returned via periodic buybacks. Core revenue +5% FY2027 fading to 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Targets met in full: ROE ~10-10.5%, ~50% TSR, full NIM pass-through, securities/WM/insurance platforms reach scale with 2028 merger synergies, benign credit through a semiconductor-led upcycle, governance remediation accepted; the stock re-rates toward KB/Shinhan multiples.
scenario_narratives.bear: Value trap: further scandal findings and a capital-hoarding regulator, a two-year domestic credit cycle (PF, SME, card) with BOK cuts compressing the CD-linked NIM, loan caps, a slipped insurance merger; ROE ~7%, payout ~30% for two years, back to 0.5-0.6x book, with won weakness on top for ADR holders.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth the equity cash flow it can distribute after funding the capital its balance sheet growth requires, discounted at the cost of equity in the flows' own currency. Woori's case rests on three things: whether the Value-up 2.0 targets (ROE ~10%, CET1 mid-to-high 13%, TSR ~50%) are delivered or merely promised; whether the 2026 rate-driven NIM uplift and record fee income persist through a credit cycle; and whether the governance scandal ends in reputation damage only or in regulator-imposed capital retention. At a 10% KRW cost of equity and a ~9% steady-state ROE the fair value is a little below book; the ADR trades at ~0.69x common book and ~8x earnings, so the gap to value is the market's discount for Korean governance and payout credibility, not for the earnings. Any valuation here is in KRW first; the USD figure moves one-for-one with the won.
key_risks_to_valuation: Governance scandal escalation: further improper-loan findings, fines or an FSS-imposed capital/payout restriction would push the realised path toward the bear case (payout ~30%, CET1 build instead of buybacks).
Credit cycle: real-estate project finance, SME and card losses (card net charge-offs already 2.6%) -- every 10bps on the ~KRW 420tn credit book is ~KRW 420bn pre-tax, ~1.1pts of margin.
Rate reversal: the CD-linked loan mix that gives ~4bps NIM per 25bps hike gives it back as fast on cuts; FY2027 base growth of 5% leans on the H2 2026 NIM expansion persisting.
KRW/USD: all flows, book and dividends are KRW; a 10% won depreciation is a 10% cut to every USD value in this file with no offset in the KRW model.
Insurance integration: the Tongyang/ABL merger (H2 2027) and the Tongyang FSC investigation; the insurers are ~9% of assets and their K-ICS capital needs could divert group capital.
Cost of equity: the 10% KRW CoE is built on an assumed ~3.5% 10Y KTB; each 1pt on the CoE is roughly +/-12% on the base value (sensitivity grid).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular NYSE close); 52-week range 48.83-84.71. Parity vs KRX 316140.KS at 1 ADS = 3 shares and KRW=X in inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: WF_Metrics.csv (29 periods FY2015-Q2 FY2026, from the 20-F/6-K filings; equity attributable to owners incl. hybrids; EPS per common share); 20-F FY2025 (consolidated income statement F-5, capital-adequacy note, equity note, Value-up section); Q2 2026 6-K (summary income statement, balance sheet, BIS/CET1 table, dividend and treasury-share tables); 20-F FY2023 and FY2022 for FY2021-22 income-statement comparatives.
data_sources.qualitative: WF_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): Q2 2026 results and guidance (CET1 13.71%, KRW 350bn 2026 buybacks, credit cost low-40bps, NIM outlook, Value-up 2.0 targets), governance scandal timeline, Tongyang/ABL acquisition and merger plan, bull/bear axes.

sanity_check_note.status: tool artefact, not a real trip
sanity_check_note.detail: scripts/sanity_check.py converts the historical USD ADR prices by MULTIPLYING by inputs.fx_rate (KRW->USD, 0.00074487) instead of dividing, so every historical 'price' lands at ~0.02-0.04 KRW and P/E and P/B round to 0.0 on both the implied and the historical side; it also has no 1 ADS = 3 shares awareness (same class as the LYG/HSBC/MFG false-pass and the CM fx-direction conflict in memory). Its 'passed: false' therefore carries no information about this valuation.

hand_computed_multiples.basis: USD ADR price / 3 x 1342.51 = KRW per common share; profit to common = NI attributable less hybrid coupons; common book = owners' equity less AT1 hybrids (KRW 48,584/share at 2026-06-30)
hand_computed_multiples.history_10yr_approx: Woori common has traded ~0.3-0.7x book and ~4-10x earnings over 2016-2025 (KRX 316140.KS / pre-2019 Woori Bank); the base value at 0.90x book sits above that range, which is the Value-up re-rating the base case assumes (ROE ~9% vs 10% CoE => ~0.9x book is the arithmetic, not a multiple assumption); neither the 2x-average P/E nor the 1.5x-maximum P/B rule would trip on correctly bridged figures.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E core net revenue = net interest income + net fees and commissions + dividend income + net insurance income, in KRW millions (12,700,000 = KRW 12.7tn; the prose below quotes bn). FY2026 (Dec year-end) is unreported: H1 2026 actual 6,300.7bn (NII 4,659.7 + net fees 1,278.8 + dividend 278.8 + net insurance 83.4, Q2 2026 6-K) + H2 2026 ~6,400bn (NIM expansion guided for H2 on the BOK hikes to 3.00%, fees at the record Q2 run-rate, both insurers now in both halves). FY2025 actual on the same definition 11,779.6bn (20-F F-5: 9,030.8 + 2,160.4 + 484.5 + 103.9); FY2024 11,282.8; FY2023 10,703.3; FY2022 10,566.8; FY2021 8,765.7. Trading/FVTPL gains, FVOCI/amortised-cost disposal gains and 'other insurance finance' are EXCLUDED (they swung from -123bn to +1,541bn between H1 2025 and H1 2026 and are largely offset inside other lines); they net into the margin, not the top line. The CSV Revenue column is empty for this ticker, so every revenue figure here comes from the filings. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027, one year from the valuation date as the engine's end-of-year discounting requires.
inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-EQUIVALENTS, not common shares. 728,090,000 common shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 6-K: 734.08m at 2025-12-31 less 5,986,638 cancelled on 2026-06-18 from the KRW 200bn H1 2026 buyback trust; treasury shares a negligible 53,945; no dilutive instruments -- basic = diluted EPS, and the long-term incentive plan is cash-settled phantom stock). Divided by 3 because 1 ADS = 3 shares of common stock (20-F cover) -> 242.70m ADS-equivalents. Held FLAT: the approved KRW 150bn H2 2026 buyback (~4.5m shares at ~KRW 33,500, c.0.6% of the count) is a distribution of the FY2026 (FY0) flow, which the model does not value, so neither the cash nor the share reduction is charged; once cancelled it lifts per-share value ~0.6%. REFRESH from the Q3 2026 6-K (due Nov 2026).
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction (house bank policy). Woori is an FSC-regulated bank holding company: customer deposits KRW 376.6tn, borrowings KRW 34.2tn and debentures are operating funding whose cost sits inside net interest income; cash and due from banks KRW 38.3tn (CSV cash_and_equivalents, 2026-06-30) is held against that funding and is not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (profit to common less the CET1 retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth) at the cost of equity, so nothing is added or deducted for debt or cash. The CSV total_debt (KRW 99.2tn at Q2 2026) is borrowings + debentures and is deliberately not used.
inputs.fcf_definition: Bank FCFE, not owner FCF. last_fcf = FY2025 shareholder distributions actually paid: common dividends KRW 927.3bn (20-F FY2025 cash flow statement 'Dividends paid') + treasury-share purchases KRW 150bn = KRW 1,077bn (1,077,000 in the file's KRW millions), 37.5% of profit to common (3,124.3 attributable less 250.2 hybrid coupons = 2,874.2). FY2026 approved distributions are higher (DPS 220/quarter vs 200, buybacks KRW 350bn vs 150bn). Forward FCFE = profit to common less the equity retention needed to hold CET1 at ~13.7% while RWA grow; the gap between that and the 35-45% TSR management guides to is capital accumulating above target, which the model treats as distributable (the Value-up 2.0 programme commits to periodic buybacks from it). Interest income is the bank's revenue, not excess-cash income, so interest_income = 0.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero treatment: Woori's share-based payments (KRW 61.6bn FY2025, 27.6bn FY2024, 20-F G&A note; CSV StockBasedComp) are a CASH-settled long-term incentive scheme ('final cash compensation is made by reflecting the stock price at the time of payment', 20-F Item 6) expensed inside G&A, i.e. already inside pre-tax profit. No equity dilution: basic and diluted EPS are identical (KRW 4,052 FY2025). Charged inside the margin, so the house and street bases coincide.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts KRW (model) to USD (quote): 1/1342.51 = 0.00074487, Yahoo Finance KRW=X 1342.51 at 2026-10-02T21:18Z. Per-share values are per ADS-equivalent (3 common shares), so intrinsic_value is USD per WF ADS, comparable to current_price; the *_krw twins are KRW per ADS; KRW per common share = *_krw / 3. Parity check: KRX 316140.KS close KRW 33,500 on 2026-10-02 x 3 / 1342.51 = US$74.86 vs the NYSE WF close at price_as_of / current_price (ADR ~0.5% above local, the later US close). A 1:1 ratio would imply US$25; the CSV's EPS (KRW 4,052 FY2025) is per common share, so per-ADS EPS = KRW 12,156 = US$9.05.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single KRW cost of equity 10.0% across all scenarios (risk charged once, via the scenario weights). Built in the flows' own currency: 10-year Korea Treasury Bond ~3.4-3.6% (ASSUMPTION, not fetched; BOK base rate raised to 3.00% in 2026 per Analysis.json) + beta ~1.1 to KOSPI x Korea ERP ~5.8-6.0% = ~9.8-10.2%. Korean bank groups' own Value-up disclosures use a ~10% cost of equity, and the house precedent for Asian ADR banks is 9-10% (MFG 9.0% JPY, HDB/IBN in INR). A USD rate (UST 10Y ~5.3%) would overcharge the KRW flows by the rate differential; the USD translation risk is carried by fx_rate and the bear weight, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: branch rent and IFRS 16 depreciation/interest on lease liabilities (KRW 18.3bn interest FY2025) sit inside G&A / operating expenses, i.e. inside pre-tax profit. lease_cost_pct_path = 0, no lease liability in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the flow: the margin is calibrated to net income attributable to owners (after NCI, KRW 103.2bn FY2025 / 57.0bn H1 2026, mostly the 22-25% minority in Tongyang Life until the August 2025 share exchange and other subsidiaries) LESS hybrid-security coupons (KRW 250.2bn FY2025; AT1 hybrids of KRW 3,511bn sit inside 'owners' equity' and their distributions are charged to retained earnings, not to net income). Neither NCI nor the hybrids is deducted again in the bridge.
inputs.engine_mapping: revenue = core net revenue (see base_revenue_definition); 'ebitda margin' = pre-tax profit to common (after credit costs, G&A, other operating expense, non-operating items, NCI and hybrid coupons) as % of core revenue -- FY2025 actual 32.5% (2,874.2 / (1-0.2109) / 11,779.6 on the 21.1% effective rate) or 32.1% re-based to a 25% rate; FY2026E 31.5% = 3,000 / 0.75 / 12,700 (H1 2026: 1,608.9 attributable - ~120 hybrid coupons = 1,489 to common, 31.5% on a 25% rate); da_pct 0 (depreciation KRW 1,250.6bn is already inside pre-tax profit, IT/branch capex is maintenance funded within it); cash tax 25% (effective 25.3% FY2023, 24.9% FY2024, 21.1% FY2025 flattered by tax-audit deferred adjustments, 23.1% H1 2026 which management says includes a 'corporate tax base effect'; statutory 26.4% incl. local tax); 'capex' = CET1 retention; wc 0; 'wacc' = KRW cost of equity. Implied multiples at the weighted value are checked by hand in KRW per common share against common book value/share KRW 48,584 (35,373.6bn / 728.09m) and TBV/share KRW 47,137 (less intangibles and goodwill 1,053.8bn).
inputs.capital_anchor: CET1 capital ~KRW 33.5tn at 2026-06-30 (13.71% x RWA 244,275bn, Q2 2026 6-K preliminary; end-2025 CET1 30,222.7bn / RWA 234,542.1bn = 12.89%, 20-F; end-2024 12.13%). Projected end-2026 CET1 ~KRW 34.0tn on ~2% H2 RWA growth. Management's medium-term target is 'mid-to-high 13%', the Value-up 2.0 programme's TSR step-ups were keyed to 12.5% and 13.0%. Retention = prior-year CET1 x that year's RWA growth; the ratio is held at ~13.7% in base and bull, built towards ~14.2% in bear.
inputs.data_quality_warning: Metrics CSV: Revenue column empty (bank; use NII + fees from the filings); OperatingCashFlow swings between -6.1tn and +18.6tn with deposit/trading flows and is NOT a cash-generation measure; ShareholdersEquity excludes NCI but INCLUDES KRW 3.5tn of AT1 hybrids (strip them for common equity); EPS is KRW per COMMON share (x3 for per-ADS); SharesOutstanding is common shares in millions (divide by 3 for ADS-equivalents). sanity_check.py has no ADS-ratio awareness (see LYG/HSBC/MFG memory): any P/E or P/B it prints from the CSV will be ~3x the real figure unless it bridges both fx and the ADS ratio.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (MFG, HBAN, LYG, HDB, IBN, HSBC, BMO, USB, WFC, NAB.AX). First valuation of this ticker, no MEMORY.md entry. Not an owner-FCF DCF: deposits are operating funding, OCF is meaningless, net debt is zero by construction and no debt or cash is bridged. Qualitative context from WF_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): Q2 2026 net income above KRW 1tn for the first time, record fee income, CET1 13.71%, KRW 350bn 2026 buybacks, FY2026 credit-cost guidance low-40bps (-15% YoY), NIM expansion on BOK hikes; risks are the 2024-25 improper-loan governance scandal and supervisory overhang, the Tongyang/ABL integration (merger H2 2027), household-loan growth caps and KRW translation for ADR holders.

bear.growth_rationale: BOK reverses to cuts in 2027 on a weak domestic economy, compressing the CD-linked book's NIM as fast as it expanded; household-loan caps and higher mortgage risk weights hold loan growth near 1-2%; fee growth stalls with capital markets; insurance integration slips past H2 2027.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit cycle: real-estate project-finance, SME and card losses push the credit cost ratio to 65-75bps in FY2027-28 (FY2023 was ~57bps), NIM compression, integration costs and fines (Tongyang FSC investigation, Woori Card data breach, further improper-loan findings) land in the same years; ROE on common equity ~7-7.5%. Partial recovery to 28% as provisions normalise.
bear.capex_rationale: Heavier retention: RWA grow 4% in FY2027-28 (won depreciation inflating KRW-equivalent FX assets, higher mortgage risk weights) and the FSS pushes CET1 up ~0.5pt to ~14.2% (an extra ~KRW 625bn a year for two years), then 3% RWA growth FY2029-31 and 2% = terminal thereafter. Payout falls to ~30% of profit to common in FY2027-28 (FY2025 actual was 37.5%), recovering to ~70% at steady state.
bear.narrative: The Korean-bank-value-trap case: the governance scandal brings further findings, fines and a regulator that wants more capital rather than more buybacks; a domestic downturn (real estate PF, SME, card) lifts credit costs for two years while BOK cuts compress NIM; the Tongyang/ABL merger slips and absorbs management; loan growth is capped. Woori stays the least profitable of the Big Four at a ~7% ROE, pays out ~30% for two years, and the stock settles back toward the 0.5-0.6x book Korean banks traded at before Value-up. KRW weakness against the dollar compounds the loss for ADR holders (not modelled in the KRW flows; carried by the bear weight).

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +5%: ~8bps of NIM from the two 2026 BOK hikes (~4bps per 25bps on the CD-linked book) on ~KRW 400tn of interest-earning assets, loan growth ~3% under the 1.5% H2 2026 household cap and stressed DSR, fees +6% off the record KRW 700bn/quarter base, full-year insurance. Fades to 2.5% = terminal, in line with Korean nominal GDP ~3-4% less a mature, capped domestic loan market.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax profit to common / core revenue. FY2026E 31.5%. Credit cost ratio guided to the low-40bps range (FY2025 impairment 2,103bn was ~50bps and included a 2025 provision top-up), G&A growth below revenue after the FY2025 securities-firm systems spend, giving ~32.5% by FY2028 (ROE on common equity ~9.0-9.5%, management ROE ~9.5-10% on its own definition); gives back a point from FY2031 as a normal credit cycle is averaged in. Steady state ROE ~9% against a 10% CoE, i.e. ~0.9x book.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retention, not capex: prior-year CET1 capital x RWA growth for the year (3.5%, 3.5%, 3.0%, 3.0%, 3.0%, then 2.5% = terminal growth), expressed as % of that year's core revenue. CET1 opens at ~KRW 34.0tn (end-2026E) and is held at ~13.7% of RWA, so terminal-year retention equals CET1 x g (KRW 1,098bn on revenue 17,651bn). Resulting total payout ~63% of profit to common in FY2027 rising to ~74% by FY2036, above the 35-45% TSR management guides for FY2026 but consistent with holding CET1 flat at target; the difference is capital the Value-up 2.0 programme says it will return through periodic buybacks.
base.terminal_note: Gordon growth governs (FCFE multiple (1+g)/(CoE-g) = 12.75x bear, 13.7x base, 14.7x bull); the 16x cap is set above all three so it does not bind. A 12x cap would have silently cut the base TV ~12%.
base.narrative: Woori delivers its Value-up 2.0 plan at a modest discount to its own targets: ROE on common equity settles around 9-9.5% rather than the 10% ambition, as the 2026 BOK hikes lift NIM, fee income keeps compounding from the securities/WM/card platforms, the two life insurers merge on schedule in H2 2027 and start contributing from 2028, and credit costs settle in the low-40bps range. Core revenue grows 5% in FY2027 fading to 2.5%; CET1 is held around 13.7% so distributions rise from ~37% of earnings (FY2025) toward ~65-75% as capital accumulation above target is returned through the committed periodic buybacks. The governance scandal costs reputation and supervisory attention but no material capital.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM expands a further ~10bps as the full rate pass-through lands, fee income sustains double-digit growth on the securities buildout, the merged insurer grows premiums, SE Asian retail compounds; loan growth at the top of the regulatory cap.
bull.margin_rationale: Value-up targets actually met: credit cost ratio ~40bps, cost-income ratio down ~3pts on branch/IT rationalisation and insurance synergies from 2028, ROE on common equity ~10-10.5% (management's ~10% ROE / ~13% ROTCE on its own definitions). Gives back a point late as a normal cycle is averaged in.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention on faster RWA growth (4.0%, 4.0%, 3.5%, 3.5%, 3.5%, then 3.0% = terminal) at a 13.7% CET1 from the same KRW 34.0tn opening base, as % of bull revenue; terminal retention = CET1 x g.
bull.narrative: The Value-up re-rating case: Woori hits its ~10% ROE / ~13% ROTCE / ~50% TSR targets, the BOK tightening cycle delivers the full NIM pass-through, the securities and asset-management platforms reach scale, the Tongyang/ABL merger closes in H2 2027 with capital and channel synergies, and credit costs stay benign through a semiconductor-led Korean upcycle. Capital generation above a 13.7% CET1 is returned in full, so buybacks step up every year. Governance remediation under the re-appointed chairman is accepted by the FSS and the scandal fades.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% and bull cut from 35% to 25%. Bear up: an unresolved governance/improper-loan scandal with the FSS explicitly conditioning the chairman's second term on remediation, an open FSC investigation at Tongyang Life, Korea's history of regulators overriding bank payout plans, a domestic credit cycle (real-estate PF, SME, card charge-offs already rising to 2.6%) and KRW translation risk that the KRW discount rate does not carry. Bull down: the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once (full NIM pass-through, insurance merger on time with synergies, benign credit, a governance all-clear and a Korean re-rating) and Woori has been the weakest of the Big Four on every one of them for a decade. Base at 50%: the capital position (CET1 13.71%) and the committed 2026 buybacks make the central path the most likely.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure
